record.rationale:
Payment detail route may not enforce payment ownership. get_payment resolves the payment by id and returns it without calling require_owner, while every sibling resource route (get_customer, get_refund, create_refund) calls require_owner before returning. The handler has the same authentication dependency as its siblings, so the difference is the ownership condition, not authentication.

Expected invariant: A customer can read only payments they own; another customer's payment is reported as...

attack.rationale: The executed check retrieved another identity's resource through a network-reachable HTTP route of the application. ATT&CK T1190 covers exploiting a weakness in an Internet-facing application; whether the route is actually Internet-facing in production is not known to the platform, hence 'proposed' and medium confidence.

steps.description: An authenticated customer requests a payment id belonging to another customer and receives the payment record.
The record exposes the amount, currency and description of another customer's payment.

preconditions: knowledge of another customer's payment id
record.impact_summary: financial payment records of other customers are readable

record.summary: The payment-detail handler returns the payment without calling require_owner, the ownership check every sibling resource route applies.

record.strategy: Call require_owner(p.customer_id, customer) in get_payment before returning the payment, exactly as the sibling resource routes do, so a payment owned by another customer is reported as not found. This reuses the existing helper, so no new abstraction is introduced.
constraints: the owner must keep read access to their own payment
every /payments route must keep requiring a valid bearer token
record.test_plan: must fail before: a non-owner requesting another customer's payment detail is refused | must pass after: a non-owner receives 404 for another customer's payment detail; the owner still receives 200 for their own payment

record.rationale:
Payment detail route may not enforce payment ownership. get_payment resolves the payment by id and returns it without calling require_owner, while every sibling resource route (get_customer, get_refund, create_refund) calls require_owner before returning. The handler has the same authentication dependency as its siblings, so the difference is the ownership condition, not authentication.

Expected invariant: A customer can read only payments they own; another customer's payment is reported as...

attack.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack.rationale: The executed check retrieved another identity's resource through a network-reachable HTTP route of the application. ATT&CK T1190 covers exploiting a weakness in an Internet-facing application; whether the route is actually Internet-facing in production is not known to the platform, hence 'proposed' and medium confidence.

steps.description: An authenticated customer requests a payment id belonging to another customer and receives the payment record.
The record exposes the amount, currency and description of another customer's payment.

preconditions: knowledge of another customer's payment id
record.impact_summary: financial payment records of other customers are readable

record.summary: The payment-detail handler returns the payment without calling require_owner, the ownership check every sibling resource route applies.

record.strategy: Call require_owner(p.customer_id, customer) in get_payment before returning the payment, exactly as the sibling resource routes do, so a payment owned by another customer is reported as not found. This reuses the existing helper, so no new abstraction is introduced.
constraints: the owner must keep read access to their own payment
every /payments route must keep requiring a valid bearer token
record.test_plan: must fail before: a non-owner requesting another customer's payment detail is refused | must pass after: a non-owner receives 404 for another customer's payment detail; the owner still receives 200 for their own payment

d3fend.name: Access Mediation
d3fend.rationale: Centralising the object-ownership check in one dependency used by every route makes the application grant or deny each request for a resource; D3FEND defines Access Mediation as 'the process of granting or denying specific requests to obtain and use information'.

record.recommendation: Make require_owner a FastAPI dependency (or wrap the store lookups in a helper that takes the current customer), so a resource route cannot be written without the ownership check.
Add a test that walks every resource route in the OpenAPI schema and asserts a non-owner identity is refused, so a new route cannot ship without the check.

patch.rationale: Call require_owner(p.customer_id, customer) in get_payment before returning the payment, exactly as the sibling resource routes do, so a payment owned by another customer is reported as not found. This reuses the existing helper, so no new abstraction is introduced.

+
